\section{Data, splits and chronology}\label{app:data}

% DRAFT-TEXT: review (connecting prose; every value is generated from the committed files named, mainly paper2/revision/datasplit_results.json, written by F-90 without training)
Values below come from \texttt{F-90} (S-91; descriptive, no training), which reads the competition files through the committed data path, and from the committed code lines quoted. The competition files themselves are not redistributed.

\paragraph{(a) The PC anchor.} The anchor is the measured conductivity of a pure-PC electrolyte with the same salt, from the same source article, at the row's concentration and temperature; it is not neat PC solvent. Per row it is looked up by (source article, salt) among the 13 pure-PC series of the training file, then interpolated: temperature at the series' grid level within 0.3 K, otherwise linearly in $1/T$ between levels (anchored rows: T level 2069); concentration linearly in the article's native unit (c interpolated (linear) 1800, c on grid 269); never extrapolated. Code: \texttt{F-91}:40 (S-01): \texttt{def anchor\_value(series, c, T):}; \texttt{F-91}:15 (S-01): \texttt{T\_TOL = 0.3  \# K, same grid level}. Anchor information and held-out rows: the pure-PC rows only supply anchors and are in no fold's training or test set. For fold A, the 100 pure-PC rows of fold A's own source article supply its anchors, so a held-out row's anchor comes from the same article as the row. DEC test anchors use same-salt pure-PC series from a fixed list of six training articles, for mol/kg test rows only, averaged where several cover (\texttt{F-91}:98 (S-01): \texttt{te\_series = \{s: [v for (d, salt), v in series.items() if salt == s and d in SAME\_SOURCE] for s in TEST\_SALTS\}}). The input scaler is a min--max map fitted on the anchored training rows and the anchored DEC test rows' inputs (no labels).

\paragraph{(b) Target.} $\log_{10}$ of the conductivity $k$ in mS/cm (\texttt{log\_k} equals $\log_{10} k$ on every training row: True). No conductivity is zero or negative (minimum 1.78e-15 mS/cm); the 45 training rows below 0.01 mS/cm are dropped (\texttt{F-91}:70 (S-01): \texttt{tr = tr[tr.k >= 0.01].reset\_index(drop=True)}), and submitted predictions are clipped at $\log_{10} k \geq -2.0$.

\paragraph{(c) Composition.} $x_{\mathrm{co}}$ is one minus the PC mole fraction, from the file's mole-fraction column; the competition file converts weight- and volume-basis sources to mole fractions (anchored training rows by source basis: w 1779, v 290). Mixtures with more than one co-solvent enter through mole-weighted co-solvent descriptors (dielectric constant, log viscosity, molar mass of the non-PC part) and mole-weighted mixture descriptors (anchored rows by number of solvents: 2 1859, 3 94, 4 116). Molality is native for mol/kg sources and $c/\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}$ for mol/L sources, with an ideal-mixing density that neglects the salt (\texttt{F-92}:52 (S-01): \texttt{\# molality: native for mol/kg; for mol/L approx c / rho\_mix (neglects salt mass)}); anchored training rows by unit: mol/kg 1779, mol/L 290; anchored DEC test rows: mol/kg 5313, all binary.

\paragraph{(f) DEC.} The test file has no conductivity column (\texttt{k}: False, \texttt{log\_k}: False); all 5959 test rows contain DEC and no training row does. The labels are held by the challenge and were never available to us; this is recorded in the competition's metadata file (\texttt{k}: ``Absent from F-93'') and in \texttt{F-31} (S-87): ``The DEC test labels are hidden''. No DEC number in this paper is an accuracy.

\paragraph{(g) Selection chronology.} The 107 epochs used by every KAN-$\delta$ model were chosen on held-out folds: in \texttt{F-02} (S-01) each of 5 seeds was early-stopped on fold A and on a second fold (EC+PC) using that fold's own held-out rows (\texttt{F-02}:209: \texttt{for s in SEEDS:  \# early stop on this fold (as specified; optimistic)}), and the median of the 10 best epochs was fixed for refits. The committed log (\texttt{F-94}, S-01): \texttt{A: PC+EA done (KAN-delta best epochs [103, 111, 138, 73, 129], VTF-KAN best epochs [21, 20, 43, 26, 22])}; \texttt{B: EC+PC done (KAN-delta best epochs [4, 116, 85, 31, 111], VTF-KAN best epochs [400, 145, 399, 400, 400])}; \texttt{median best epochs: KAN-delta 107, VTF-KAN 94}. \textbf{Fold A was therefore reused during development: it informed the epoch count, and the committed studies below evaluated on it before the paper's final comparisons.} The list is every committed output or pre-registration that reports on fold A, by the commit that added it.
